note_tweet.text:
$META | Muse Voice Is Just the Beginning. Is Meta Building the Next Consumer Computing Platform?
Meta has rolled out Muse Voice to all Muse users in the US, enabling real-time voice conversations with its AI agent.

Users can now talk naturally with Muse instead of typing instructions. Even more interestingly, Muse can launch sub-agents and begin working on tasks before the user finishes speaking.

But I don't see this as just another voice feature.

1. AI Is Moving Beyond the Chat Interface

Until now, using AI has generally meant opening an app, typing a prompt, and waiting for a response.

Muse Voice begins to remove that friction.

People can interact with AI while driving, cooking, or simply thinking out loud. Instead of setting aside time to use AI, they can increasingly integrate it into everyday life.

The real shift isn't just smarter AI. It's making AI available whenever people need it, without interrupting what they're doing.

2. The Next Step: Muse Meets Meta's Smart Glasses

Meta has already announced plans to bring Muse to its AI smart glasses.

I think this combination could be particularly powerful.

Today, AI agents primarily understand our digital lives through conversations, calendars, emails, and other connected information.

Smart glasses could extend that understanding into the physical world.

Imagine looking at a product in a store and asking:

"Will this work with the equipment I already have at home? Is there a better or cheaper alternative?"

An AI agent could combine what you're looking at with your purchase history and personal preferences, compare alternatives, and potentially help complete the purchase.

Voice communicates your intent. Smart glasses provide real-world context. AI agents turn that understanding into action.

That's a much more compelling experience than simply chatting with an AI model.

3. Meta Has an Opportunity to Build a New Consumer Platform

One of Meta's long-standing weaknesses has been its dependence on Apple and Google's operating systems and hardware ecosystems.

But Muse and smart glasses could gradually change that relationship.

Meta already has enormous consumer reach through Facebook, Instagram, and WhatsApp.

Now imagine combining those platforms with:

Muse: An AI agent that understands users' personal context.

AI infrastructure: Computing capacity that powers increasingly capable agents.

Smart glasses: A direct interface between AI and the physical world.

Investments that once appeared separate—AI, the metaverse, and AR hardware—could begin to form a connected ecosystem.

If smart glasses become a mainstream way to interact with AI, Meta could establish a more direct relationship with consumers, reducing its dependence on smartphone platforms.

Of course, this outcome is far from guaranteed. Apple and Google have deeply established ecosystems, while smart glasses still face challenges involving comfort, battery life, privacy, and inference costs.

4. The Moat I'm Watching

As AI models become increasingly capable, I believe competitive advantages could gradually shift toward who understands users best and who can deliver useful AI experiences across the most everyday situations.

Meta has an interesting combination of assets:

Social relationships through its existing platforms, personal context through Muse, and potentially real-world awareness through smart glasses.

Together, these could create an ecosystem that becomes more useful as people interact with it throughout their day.

I see Muse Voice as an early step toward that possibility.

Meta's biggest opportunity may not be building the smartest chatbot. It may be owning both the personal AI agent people rely on throughout the day and the next-generation hardware they use to interact with it.

If that vision succeeds, Meta won't just be competing with OpenAI and Anthropic.

It could also challenge part of the consumer computing platform dominance that Apple and Google have enjoyed for years.

What do you think? Could AI smart glasses eventually become as important as smartphones?

This post is not a recommendation to buy or sell any particular asset.

$META

今日のAI、これだけ押さえとけばOK。
Anthropicのエンジニア自身が「使いすぎるな」と言い出した日だ。

①Anthropic自身が「cognitive surrender(認知的降伏)」に警鐘
AIを作ってる側の人間が「依存しすぎると思考力が死ぬ」と警告した。逆説的すぎて笑えるけど、これが一番刺さる話だと思う。僕は毎日15時間AIと一緒に仕事してるから人ごとじゃない。正直、「考えなくても答えが出る」快適さに慣れていくのは実感としてある。ただ、AIに思考を丸投げするのと、AIを道具として使い倒すのは全然違う。「自分が判断してAIに実行させる」の順番を崩さないことだけ意識してる。

②Y Combinator元代表のGarry Tanが「gstack」を公開
Claude Codeを「仮想エンジニアチーム」として動かすための環境設定をそのままオープンソースで公開した。GitHubトレンド入り。設定ファイルを公開する透明性がいい。「1人でチーム相当の出力を出す」という今の時代を象徴してるネタで、僕もClaude CodeとcodexをメインでXの自動投稿システムから動画制作まで回してるから、この設定の中身は普通に気になってる。週末に触る。

③Meta Muse Wonder派生モデルを無料ユーザーにも全展開
重要情報の忘却率が2.4倍改善、日常タスクの自己修正精度が67%向上と主張。有料モデルの恩恵を無料層に流すのはChatGPTへの流出を食い止める露骨な戦略だけど、使う側からすれば純粋にありがたい。ただMetaのAI発表は「主張の数字が大きすぎる」印象がずっとあるので、自分で触って判断するのが先。

④OpenAI×Hacktronでセキュリティ強化——攻撃面の急拡大を公式に認めた
AIがサードパーティと深く統合される時代、接続部分の脆弱性が一気に増えてる。「第三者連携の弱いところを一緒に探す」体制を組んだということは、裏を返せば今ここが一番危ういと自分たちも認識してる。エージェントを使う時に権限の範囲を絞る話は何度か書いてきたけど、今日の件でまた現実感が出た。

⑤GPT-6 Cyber——防御側の研究者に限定公開
サイバーセキュリティ特化モデルがDaybreak Redプログラム経由で出た。先週GPT-6 Cyberが81件の脆弱性を自動発見したというニュースを書いたけど、今日はそのモデルが実際に防御側の手に渡りはじめた話。AIが「攻撃も防御も両方やれる」存在になってきた。セキュリティの常識が今年だけでかなり変わってる。

今日イチは③より①だと思う。道具を作ってる側が「使いすぎるな」と言った重さは、ちゃんと受け取っておくべきだ。また明日まとめる。
